meter_schema.why_it_is_here: This file shipped with zero occurrences of the strings 'meter' and 'estimate' while the dataset defines 33 meters, every one of which carries provenance (sourceClass), a value state (vs), a confidence (conf) and an explanatory note - and one of which carries a user-visible estimated percentage with its own basis and confidence. A user-facing estimate governed by no clause in the required event and schema output is an undeclared contract. Audit finding A11-15.
meter_schema.scoping_note: Meters are provider-native quota state (packet section 01) rather than events, so a case can be made that an event-schema delta need not carry them. That case is weakened by this same file already declaring the non-event collections hosts[] and environments[]. The meter schema is declared here because meters are the surface on which the packet's 'unknown displayed as zero' hard failure actually lives.

fields.productId: products[].id - the plan or product whose allowance this meter measures
fields.label: user-visible name of the allowance
fields.unit: the unit the allowance is counted in (credits, requests, tokens, runtime, ...)
fields.windowKind: the reset window shape (billing_cycle, rolling_5h, weekly, session_only, none, ...)
fields.used: int | null - null means not known and is never rendered as zero
fields.limit: int | null - null means not exposed or not knowable, never zero
fields.usedPct: int | null - null means not known and is never rendered as zero
fields.vs: value state of the figure - see value_state_enum
fields.settlement: source-quality of the settlement fact, same domain as on attempts
fields.conf: confidence in the figure where it is not directly reported
fields.note: human explanation rendered beside the figure whenever the value state is not a plain reported number
fields.estimate: optional object, present only when the provider figure is unavailable and PM computes one - see estimate_object
fields.expiresAt: ISO UTC | null - optional; present on 3 of 33 meters. When the allowance itself expires, as distinct from resetAt, which is when the window rolls.
fields.sourceAuthority: string | absent - optional; present on 4 of 33. The named authority behind the figure, in words, where sourceClass alone is not specific enough.
fields.pressure: object | absent - optional; present on 2 of 33. The precomputed pressure band for the row, so a renderer does not re-derive it from usedPct.
fields.quotaStatus: string | absent - optional; present on 2 of 33. The CLI-bridged quota state (reported | disabled | not_exposed), shared with the CBP-027 quota vocabulary.
fields.evidenceSource: string | absent - optional; present on 2 of 33. Which read produced the figure (cli_command, provider_api, not_exposed).
fields.allowanceAttribution: string | absent - optional; present on 2 of 33. Which allowance a draw-down was attributed to, where more than one could claim it.

estimate_object.instance: meter:oc-go-monthly carries { usedPct: 63, basis: 'PM history · last 7 days', conf: 'medium' } with vs 'unavailable' and note 'Provider ready · Usage details unavailable'.
estimate_object.user_visible_rendering: 'Provider data unavailable · PM estimate 63% · medium confidence' in the Plans and limits widget
estimate_object.contract: An estimate object may be present only when vs is 'unavailable' or 'estimated'. It must carry its own basis and confidence. The rendered copy must attribute the figure to PM rather than to the provider. It must never substitute for a provider figure that exists, and it must never be rendered as zero.
estimate_object.verification_basis: The harness case 'new plans estimate (unavailable -> PM estimate 63%)' waits for that exact string in document.body.innerText, so the rendered copy is DOM-verified for this one meter. No harness case checks the contract's other clauses, and no other meter carries an estimate, so the contract is declared here and demonstrated once.
estimate_object.open_question: Audit finding A07-02 notes that packet 04 specifies the exact string 'Provider ready · Usage details unavailable' for this state, and demo-fixture-report.json records the concept's own different copy as a pass without noting the divergence. The meter's note field does carry the packet string; the widget renders its own. Which is authoritative is not settled here.

values.meaning: the provider reported the figure directly
PM measured it locally from receipts
a real figure, older than the freshness window
the figure is not knowable from any source - never rendered as zero
the meter exists but the route is turned off
PM computed the figure; an estimate object must accompany it
the provider has the figure but does not expose it - distinct from unknown and from zero
provider telemetry is temporarily unavailable; an estimate object may accompany it

corrections_2026_08_18.why_the_claim_was_false: The block was added on 2026-08-18 to close A11-15 and declared 15 of the 21 keys the meters actually carry. Six optional keys - expiresAt, sourceAuthority, pressure, quotaStatus, evidenceSource and allowanceAttribution - were undeclared, and two of them (quotaStatus, evidenceSource) belong to the CBP-027 vocabulary this same concept renders. A schema block that declares most of a shape reads as if it declares all of it, which is the failure mode A11-15 named in the first place.

purpose_taxonomy.rendering_caveat: Added 2026-08-18. R().human is _shared/usage-data.js:921, `String(s).replace(/_/g, ' ')`. Because it strips underscores at render time, the harness's 'zero underscores in any text node' assertion cannot detect a raw enum token leaking into user-visible copy - the token simply renders de-underscored and passes. That is why renaming the entire purpose taxonomy required zero renderer edits, and it is a limitation of the check, not a property of the copy.

Plans/settings_inventory.json has 12 categories (general, ai, safety, code, memory, planning, branching, media, web, personas, extensions, system) and neither 'providers' nor 'usage' is one of them - 'providers' exists only as a subgroup of web, meaning web-search providers, and 'usage' only as a subgroup of ai. The tokens focus_reason, usage_and_extra_usage, usage_quick_controls and see_all have zero occurrences anywhere under Plans/ (measured 2026-08-18). The canonical contract is F3-434's open(category, focusSettingId), bound to cmd.settings.bloom.open and certified at Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json row catalog.settings_bloom_open.
operational[].setupLink_correction.known_gap: The ops-8 record in u11-data.js still carries the legacy setupLink keys and reaches the canonical row through LEGACY_DEST_MAP in U11.deepLink. Migrating the data to the canonical shape is a concept-side change and is not part of this register repair. The contract declared above is the canonical one; the data has not yet caught up to it, and this register says so rather than describing the legacy shape as if it were the contract.

production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.finding: A11-22 (info) - closed as recorded, not as repaired.
production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.statement: Nothing proposed in this file has a production wiring row that would carry it as a domain event. All five usage rows in Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json - catalog.usage_refresh, catalog.usage_export, catalog.usage_forecast_request, catalog.nav_open_usage_subject and catalog.artifacts_show_in_usage - carry expected_event_types []. 160 of the matrix's 726 entries declare event types; none of the usage ones does.
production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.what_the_rows_do_declare: effect_kind 'receipt'. catalog.usage_refresh states it outright: 'cmd.usage.refresh has no declared persisted event; dispatch must still record a no-persist command receipt or route/open disposition.' So the shapes in this file are receipt and projection shapes, not event payloads.
production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.denominator: Plans/DRY_Rules.md ':2139', in the section 'Unresolved schema and Event Authority boundary' (:2132-2143): 'The Event Authority denominator remains UNKNOWN_OPEN. No event family is inferred, registered, or declared emitted from a service name in this registry.' Admitting a usage event family is an Event Authority adjudication. This file does not perform one and does not name a candidate family, because naming one would be exactly the inference that clause forbids.
production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.how_to_read_this_file_until_then: attempt_schema, meter_schema, the four new collections and the id renumbers are proposals against a receipt-and-projection contract. They are not evidence that a usage event family exists, and the word 'event' in this file's own name should not be read as one.
production_wiring_and_event_authority_20.scope_note: Plans/** is read-only to this concept; nothing there was edited.

items: No migration or supersession register exists in reports/ at all. id_renumbers is a change log entry, not a migration contract.

The cacheStats[] row shape is declared only in candidate-dry-delta.json's CacheReceipt role string, not here, even though it carries its own state enum (measured | estimated | unsupported) and its own null-versus-zero semantics.

The client-persistence contract for the five localStorage keys lives in impact-register.json storage_retention_impacts, not here. Whether persisted client state belongs in an event-schema delta is an open packet question.

source_citation_policy: Source citations into u11-prism.html, u11-data.js, u11-widgets.js, u11-rundetail.js and u11-context.js name a symbol, identifier or exact string rather than a line number. Those five files were under concurrent edit on 2026-08-18 - u11-data.js moved twice while this repair was being written - so a line number here would be wrong by the time it was read. Line numbers are retained only for files that are stable in this pass: everything under Plans/ and under _shared/. Text preserved inside a `retraction` or `retracted_claim` object is left exactly as it was written, line numbers included, because its purpose is to record what a document said on a past date.
